Validation results from a real local run against Victor's WKG on the PGlite branch.

Environment
- macOS 26.4
- Apple M4 (10 cores)
- 24 GB RAM

Dataset
- Repo: `~/ws/wkg`
- 6655 markdown files
- 30.82 MB total markdown text (`.md` only)
- 629 MB repo size on disk including crawl/tmp/log artifacts

PGlite / local DB
- Config used: `engine=pglite`, `database_path=~/.gbrain/brain.db`
- Actual persisted store is `~/.gbrain/brain.db.pglite`
- Existing main local DB size: ~238 MB
- Fresh benchmark DB after full import: ~237 MB

What was verified
1. `gbrain init --pglite ...` succeeds
2. schema migration succeeds
3. `vector` + `pg_trgm` extensions are available in PGlite mode
4. full import of WKG into a fresh local PGlite DB succeeds
5. keyword search works
6. query embedding + hybrid query also works once `OPENAI_API_KEY` is actually exported into the shell

Fresh full import benchmark (temporary PGlite DB, `--no-embed --fresh`)
- Pages imported: 6653
- Chunks created: 13445
- Time: 10.9 s wall clock
- Throughput: ~610 pages/s, ~1233 chunks/s
- Peak RSS during import: ~847 MB

Keyword search benchmark (end-to-end CLI latency, includes bun startup + PGlite bridge)
- `gbrain search "Faculty Group"` -> ~0.20 s avg (5/5 runs were 0.20 s)
- `gbrain search "Slow Ventures"` -> ~0.206 s avg, max 0.25 s
- `gbrain search "zk proofs marketplace"` -> ~0.196 s avg
- `gbrain stats` -> ~0.17 s avg
- Peak RSS for a sample search: ~449 MB

Hybrid query validation
Notes:
- `query` does NOT auto-read `~/.env`; the shell must export the env vars (`set -a; source ~/.env; set +a`)
- with no embeddings in the DB, `query` will not give useful results even if the OpenAI key exists

Small live validation run:
- `gbrain embed investors/faculty-group` -> `embedded 1 chunks`
- `gbrain query "what do we know about Faculty Group" --no-expand` -> returns `investors/faculty-group`
- `gbrain query "investor behind Auki Labs" --no-expand` -> returns `investors/faculty-group`
- `gbrain query "computer vision investor fund" --no-expand` -> also surfaces `investors/faculty-group`
- query latency in this partially embedded state: ~0.45 s to ~0.82 s end-to-end over a few runs

Bottom line
- The PGlite branch is no longer just a theory/demo; it works against a real ~6.6k-page WKG on local hardware.
- For the current gbrain DB workload, PGlite is a viable substitute for external Postgres/Supabase for local setup, import, persistence, keyword search, and hybrid query.

Remaining caveats are mostly product/ergonomics, not DB viability:
- `query` should probably fall back cleanly when there is no OpenAI key / no embeddings
- CLI does not auto-load `~/.env` or `~/.hermes/.env`
- import is intentionally single-worker in PGlite mode, so this is validated as a local/dev path, not as a high-concurrency Postgres replacement

Hey @garrytan 👋

Quick context on why this PR exists and the design choices we made:

## Why multi-provider?

GBrain currently hardcodes OpenAI's \	ext-embedding-3-large\ everywhere — the embedding client, the DB schema (\ector(1536)\), and the config table defaults. This makes it impossible to use GBrain with any other embedding provider without forking.

We're using GBrain in China where OpenAI API access is unreliable. But this isn't just a China problem — anyone wanting to use local models (Ollama), cheaper alternatives (Gemini), or domain-specific embeddings hits the same wall.

## Design principles

1. **Zero new dependencies** — All 7 providers go through the existing OpenAI SDK by swapping \ aseURL\. DashScope, DeepSeek, Zhipu, and Gemini all offer OpenAI-compatible \/v1/embeddings\ endpoints. This keeps the dependency tree unchanged.

2. **One env var to switch** — \GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=dashscope\ and you're done. Sensible defaults for model name, dimensions, and base URL per provider.

3. **Dynamic vector dimensions** — The old \ector(1536)\ hardcode in the schema meant any non-1536-dimension model would crash on INSERT. Now it reads from \EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS\ which is resolved at startup based on the provider config.

4. **Backward compatible** — If you set nothing, it defaults to \openai\ + \	ext-embedding-3-large\ + \1536\ dimensions. Existing deployments are unaffected.

5. **\sendDimensions\ flag** — Not all providers support the \dimensions\ parameter for output truncation (DeepSeek, Zhipu, Ollama don't). We track this per provider to avoid API errors.

## What's NOT in this PR

- No migration logic for existing DBs with \ector(1536)\ columns (switching providers on an existing brain would need re-embedding anyway)
- No MiniMax support (their embedding API isn't OpenAI-compatible; users can use the \custom\ provider as a workaround)
- No Kimi/Moonshot (they don't offer a dedicated embedding model yet)

Happy to iterate on any of this. Would love to see GBrain work for the global community 🌏

Updating my earlier comment — let me rephrase the motivation more accurately:

## Why multi-provider?

GBrain currently hardcodes OpenAI's \	ext-embedding-3-large\ everywhere — the embedding client, the DB schema (\ector(1536)\), and the config table defaults. This means anyone who wants to use a different embedding provider (for cost, latency, data residency, or model preference) has to fork.

**Use cases this enables:**
- Teams that prefer to keep data on-premises (Ollama)
- Developers using Google Cloud credits (Gemini)
- Users who want cheaper embeddings (DeepSeek, DashScope)
- Enterprise deployments with specific vendor requirements (Zhipu, DashScope)
- Anyone experimenting with domain-specific embedding models (custom provider)

The rest of the design principles remain the same — zero new deps, one env var to switch, dynamic vector dimensions, full backward compatibility.

I found the cause and a workaround.

Root cause appears to be that the lock code tries to create:

<dataDir>/.gbrain-lock

before <dataDir> itself exists.

On first-time init, that means mkdirSync(lockDir, { recursive: false }) fails with ENOENT repeatedly, and the CLI eventually reports a misleading timeout:

GBrain: Timed out waiting for PGLite lock.

Workaround:
pre-create the PGLite data directory before running init.

This works for me:

```
mkdir -p ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite
cd ~/gbrain
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
```
bun run src/cli.ts init --pgliteAfter pre-creating the directory, init succeeds normally.

So the likely fix is to ensure dataDir exists before trying to create dataDir/.gbrain-lock, or otherwise change the lock path creation logic so first-run init does not fail with ENOENT.

I know this is a fairly large PR and targets a specific use case, but it may be useful for others working with Obsidian-based knowledge graphs. Right now, when importing markdown files, gbrain works great but it doesn’t preserve the link graph between notes. This PR adds support for that. In my case (~13k markdown files, ~10k links), this preserves the original graph structure instead of flattening everything: This means you can make a large Obsidian graph more efficiently searchable with gbrain, which is already a game changer for me.

Great work on this. Spotted a couple things reading the diff:

**Migration v5 can silently fail.** The DROP CONSTRAINT assumes the name is `links_from_page_id_to_page_id_key` but Postgres auto-generates constraint names and they can differ. If the name doesn't match, IF EXISTS swallows the miss, the old unique constraint stays, and inserting two typed links between the same pages breaks at runtime. Safer to drop the underlying index directly instead of relying on the constraint name.

**N+1 at scale.** reconcileLinksForPage and performObsidianLinkSync call getPage() once per link target. At 13k files and 10k links that's 23k+ sequential queries. Fine on PGLite (in-process) but on a remote Postgres instance those are 23k round-trips. Batch with WHERE slug = ANY($1) would fix it.

**dead_links changed meaning.** Old query counted links pointing to non-existent pages. New one counts chunks on empty pages. Both useful but they measure different things. Worth renaming or keeping both.

The migration is the one I'd look at first since it can break silently.

The pgvector extension in PGLite returns embeddings as string (e.g., "[0.1, 0.2]") instead of Float32Array.

In pglite-engine.ts, the code uses Array.from(chunk.embedding), which splits the string into individual characters (e.g., ["[", "0", ".", "1", ...]) when it's already a string. This results in an invalid format like "[[,0,.,1...]]" that Postgres fails to parse.

The as Float32Array cast in rowToChunk was just a type hint and didn't perform any real conversion. I'm currently fixing this.

@garagon 

Those are great catches, thank you! I fixed the migration and N+1 issues.

Migration v5 now drops the old two-column uniqueness by inspecting `pg_catalog`, not by assuming `links_from_page_id_to_page_id_key`, and there’s a regression test with a custom old constraint name.

The N+1 is also fixed: Obsidian sync and link reconciliation now batch page-existence checks through the engine interface.

On `dead_links`, agreed the name is confusing. Trialed this PR end-to-end on a 128-page Obsidian-backed vault (macOS, PGLite engine, local Ollama). Confirming the Ollama integration works — `gbrain init --ollama --embedding-model nomic-embed-text` + `gbrain embed --stale` cleanly embedded 253 chunks at 768d.

Some observations from real-world use that might be worth folding in:

### 1. Extend `OLLAMA_MODEL_DIMENSIONS` with a few more common models

```ts
const OLLAMA_MODEL_DIMENSIONS: Record<string, number> = {
  'nomic-embed-text': 768,
  'mxbai-embed-large': 1024,
  'snowflake-arctic-embed': 1024,
  'snowflake-arctic-embed2': 1024,   // top open-source English retrieval, 568M
  'bge-m3': 1024,                    // multilingual, 8k context
  'embeddinggemma': 768,             // Google's recent small-model leader
  'all-minilm': 384,
};
```

When I ran `gbrain init --ollama --embedding-model snowflake-arctic-embed2` on a clean brain, the absence of the entry made it fall through to the `|| 768` default, which then failed on insert since the model actually returns 1024d. Adding it to the table avoids users needing the `embedding_dimensions` override for these popular models.

### 2. Dynamic dimension probe via `/api/show`

For anything not in the hardcoded table, `POST http://localhost:11434/api/show` with `{"name":"<model>"}` returns `embedding_length` in the response. Example:

```
"Model":
  architecture        nomic-bert
  parameters          137M
  embedding length    768
  ...
```

Could probe this at init time if `embedding_dimensions` isn't in config, eliminating the hardcoded table entirely. Happy to open a separate PR for this if you're interested.

### 3. `halfvec` for models >4000d (qwen3-embedding:8b, etc.)

pgvector's default `vector` column + HNSW index caps at 4000 dimensions. `qwen3-embedding:8b` (4096d) is a popular, very strong open-source model that exceeds this. Your codebase already has `EmbeddingStorageType = 'vector' | 'halfvec'` — exposing a `--halfvec` init flag (or auto-selecting halfvec when `embedding_dimensions > 4000`) would unlock this.

Encountered this when trying qwen3-embedding:8b for a vault trial. Settled on snowflake-arctic-embed2 which fits comfortably in the vector+HNSW default.

Follow-up: found a third problem in the wrapper after fixing #1 and #2 above.

**3. Wrapper doesn't load Keychain-backed env vars on macOS zsh setups.**

The generated wrapper is `#!/bin/bash` + `source ~/.zshrc`. On common macOS setups, Keychain-backed exports live in `~/.zshenv` (auto-sourced by zsh for all invocations, interactive or not) rather than `~/.zshrc`. Bash sourcing `~/.zshrc` doesn't chain to `~/.zshenv`, so `$OPENAI_API_KEY` is empty in the wrapper env and every embed call throws:

```
Error embedding <slug>: The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is missing or empty
```

**Proposed fix:** switch the shebang to `#!/bin/zsh` and source both files explicitly:

```bash
#!/bin/zsh
emulate -LR zsh
[[ -f ~/.zshenv ]] && source ~/.zshenv
[[ -f ~/.zshrc ]] && source ~/.zshrc
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
exec "$HOME/.bun/bin/gbrain" autopilot --repo '...'
```

zsh auto-sources `~/.zshenv` on every invocation, which is the canonical location for env exports that need to survive non-interactive shells. This is also why `launchctl` → `bash` → `source ~/.zshrc` leaves the wrapper blind to Keychain-backed secrets that work fine from interactive terminals.

**Related finding for docs:** Supabase's _transaction_ pooler (port 6543) also breaks gbrain's embed + health paths with:

```
prepared statement "xxx" does not exist
```

because PgBouncer transaction mode discards prepared statements between queries. The **session** pooler (port 5432 with user `postgres.<ref>@aws-<n>-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`) preserves them and works fine. The `setup/SKILL.md` currently recommends port 6543, which I believe is wrong for gbrain's usage pattern — at minimum worth documenting.

Ran into this exact concern while setting up gbrain on a Hermes-agent install last night and implemented garagon's quarantine-namespace proposal as a local patch before circling back to this issue. Sharing what we built and what we learned in case it helps the design discussion.

**What triggered it for us.** During smoke testing, a synthetic message with fabricated names (fake pre-seed founder, fake girlfriend, fake company) fired through the signal-detector-equivalent we had running as a Hermes plugin. Nothing stopped the extractor from writing `people/<fake-name>.md` pages with authoritative-looking timeline entries. A PATH bug in our first plugin attempt accidentally protected us from the pollution; once we fixed the PATH bug, the same test content wrote clean pages straight into authoritative directories. That's when we came looking for prior art and found this issue.

**What we shipped:**

1. **Quarantine namespace `_pending/`.** Plugin writes to `~/brain/_pending/{type}/{slug}.md` instead of `~/brain/{type}/{slug}.md`. Authoritative dirs stay empty until something explicitly promotes from quarantine. Implemented as a 3-line exclusion in `src/core/sync.ts::isSyncable()` matching the existing `ops/` / `.raw/` pattern.

2. **Input-hash frontmatter on every quarantined page.** `<!-- input_hash=XXXXXXXXXXXX -->` where the hash is over the source message text, not the page content. Lets a blocklist target source messages rather than final page content, which matters if the same fabricated input could produce multiple page variants (regex false positives from the same text often do).

3. **72-hour age gate before any evaluation.** Gives the capture time to be contradicted or reinforced by later messages before we consider promoting.

4. **Second-pass notability evaluator (Sonnet 4.6 in our case).** Daily cron walks `_pending/`, calls a second model with a stricter prompt than signal-detector used. Criteria baked in:
   - Real entity or genuine original thinking, not a regex false positive (garagon's "Dear John", "Bar Mitzvah", "New York" are exactly the failure modes we target).
   - Enough content to be worth keeping.
   - Source attribution present.
   - For `people/` specifically: real-world anchoring plus substantive enough to identify later.

5. **Three verdicts: promote, reject, defer.** Defer increments `<!-- defer_count=N -->` frontmatter. Max 3 defer cycles (9 days) before force-reject. Gives ambiguous captures a chance to accumulate cross-references without letting them sit forever.

6. **Collision-safe promote.** Before `mv _pending/{type}/{slug} {type}/{slug}`, check target existence. If yes, defer with reason `target_exists_manual_merge_needed` rather than silently overwriting. Addresses the slug-collision class.

7. **JSONL audit log.** Every evaluation gets `{slug, age, defer_count, verdict, reason}`. `grep '"verdict":"reject"' log.jsonl | tail -20` inspects filter quality.

**Dry-run result on 175 pending pages** from a first live overnight: 101 promote / 55 reject / 19 defer / 0 errors. Sample reject reason: "Near-empty stub with no substantive content about what AGENTS.md actually contains or governs." Sample promote: "Genuine original concept with substantive definition, real-world anchoring to this system's own governance rules, and proper source attribution." One dry-run isn't real quality data, but the verdicts read sensibly on spot checks.

**On the three approaches in the issue:** we went with shape 1 (quarantine namespace) for the reasons garagon lists, but replaced the manual-review step with an auto-evaluator because our prior experience with voluntary-review protocols is that they decay. The second-pass evaluator is more work than an allow-list or a synchronous confirmation, but it keeps the ambient-capture pattern working while adding the trust boundary.

**Adjacent upstream work we cross-referenced while building this:**

- **Issue #132** (sync deadlock on incremental sync with >10 modified files): our workaround avoids the lock class entirely by writing markdown files directly and letting autopilot sync to the DB on its cycle. PR #193 (open) appears to fix the deadlock class upstream by removing the outer transaction wrapper, which is independent of our pattern.
- **Commit `ec0556a`** on branch `garrytan/minions-jobs` states in its body: "PGLite has an exclusive file lock that blocks a second worker process, so the inline path is the only path that works there." Upstream confirming the single-writer constraint is what led us to the markdown-first pattern rather than calling `gbrain put` from the plugin.
- **PR #194** (feat: configurable entity_dirs + wikilinks): the author describes hitting 0 auto-link extraction on a 2,052-page Obsidian vault because of the hardcoded entity-dir list. We hit the same 0 on 61 indexed pages of narrative prose (history files with natural-language first names in body text, no `[Name](people/name)` wiki refs). Our graph-layer output was 0 links post-install; PR #194's configurable `entity_dirs` would likely fix this.

**Honest gap in our implementation:** we write markdown files directly and let autopilot pick them up, which means the v0.10.3 auto-link post-hook on `put_page` never fires on our promoted pages. The promotion-cron's `path.rename()` from `_pending/{type}/{slug}.md` to `{type}/{slug}.md` also doesn't go through `put_page`, so back-links per the Iron Law in `skills/conventions/quality.md` don't auto-create on promote either. Fix we're about to ship in our plugin: replay `gbrain put {slug}` on the content after rename, which triggers both auto-link and back-link on the authoritative write. If the upstream version of this gate ships in TypeScript via the engine interface, this problem doesn't exist; it's an artifact of our plugin living outside the gbrain process.

**Related issues we filed** while working through the quarantine implementation (not blockers, but adjacent):
- Issue #202 (extract --source fs doesn't respect isSyncable prefix exclusions): the fs walker skips `.`-prefix and `_`-prefix FILE entries but not `_`-prefix DIRECTORIES, so `_pending/` gets walked anyway on extract.
- Issue #203 (init ignores config.json embedding defaults): relevant if `_pending/` implementations want a clean re-init path.
- Issue #204 (autopilot SIGTERM non-cancelable): relevant if the quarantine gate runs inside a long-lived daemon.

Same bug reproduces on the Postgres engine (not just PGLite). Same root cause: schema-embedded runs before migrations.

## Postgres repro

- gbrain 0.13.1 on a Supabase Postgres 17.6 brain that was at schema_version 10.
- `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` fails with:
  ```
  column "link_source" does not exist
  Migration v0.13.0 reported status=failed.
  ```

## Path in postgres-engine

`src/core/postgres-engine.ts:59-74` does:

```ts
async initSchema(): Promise<void> {
  await conn`SELECT pg_advisory_lock(42)`;
  try {
    await conn.unsafe(SCHEMA_SQL);            // <-- runs first
    const { applied } = await runMigrations(this);  // <-- too late
  } finally { ... }
}
```

`SCHEMA_SQL` is the embedded `src/schema.sql`, whose lines 81-82 declare:
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_origin ON links(origin_page_id);
```
Same story: on an existing pre-v13 brain the `links` table has not yet gained `link_source`, `origin_page_id`, or `origin_field`; those columns are added by the migration ladder at `src/core/migrate.ts:319-348` (version 11), which never runs because SCHEMA_SQL aborted. So the fix needs to land in both `pglite-schema.ts` and `src/schema.sql`, or (preferably) the ordering fix you called option (b) covers both paths in one go.

## Workaround for Postgres users

Since you can't wipe `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` here, you have to manually add the missing columns on a direct (non-pooler) connection:
```sql
ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS link_source TEXT;
ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin_page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

**`process.execPath` bug** — v0.13.0 Phase B ran `bun extract links --source db --include-frontmatter` instead of `gbrain extract ...`. ### Note on migrate.ts v12 modification

I'm aware that `migrate.ts` L39 says "Never modify existing ones." This PR adds a RLS DO block to the v12 `budget_ledger` migration, which technically violates that rule.

The trade-off:

- **New installs** get RLS on `budget_ledger` / `budget_reservations` automatically via the updated v12 SQL.
- **Existing users** who already ran v12 won't re-run it, so their budget tables stay unprotected until they either (a) run the one-shot SQL in the PR body, or (b) a new migration (e.g. v16) applies the same `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.

+  IF EXISTS (

+     WHERE table_name = 'files' AND column_name = 'source_id'

Don't forget to regenerate `src/core/schema-embedded.ts` via `bun run build:schema`.

### Verification

Tested on a production Supabase brain, 322 pages, starting schema v15:

1. **Before fix:** `gbrain init --migrate-only` → `column "page_id" does not exist`. `apply-migrations --yes` wedges v0.11.0 at Phase A (gbrain logs 3+ consecutive partials → "wedged" status in `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl`).
2. **After fix:** `gbrain init --migrate-only` walks v15 → v24 cleanly in ~3s. All 6 pending schema migrations (v16 cycle_locks → v24 rls_backfill) apply in sequence. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` then walks all 9 orchestrator migrations (v0.11.0 → v0.18.1) to `applied`. `gbrain doctor --fast` reports health 90/100.
3. **Write path confirmed working** post-migration: `mcporter call gbrain.put_page` + `add_link` + `search` / `query` all functional. Brain post-fix: 325 pages, 485 chunks, 811 links.

### Why the guard works

On fresh brains, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (...)` at schema.sql:52 defines `source_id` as part of the table, so the `information_schema.columns` lookup passes and the index is created (same behavior as before).

On upgrading brains (schema < v20), the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages` is a no-op, the column-existence check fails, and the index creation is skipped. Migration v21 then runs, adds the column via `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id`, and the migration's own `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id)` handles the index at that point.

### Aside: partial-write risk on the wedged state

Worth flagging — since the wedge happens inside `initSchema()` which is called by every `gbrain import` / sync / `put_page` flow, any user with the broken schema has been silently losing writes. In my case the Mac's `launchd`-triggered `ideas-to-brain.sh` was failing daily scans for ~2 days before I caught it. No data corruption (writes just error out cleanly), but worth a note in the release wave that fixes this.

## Workaround Applied

After further investigation, I implemented a kill-old-then-start-new wrapper script at `/root/.bun/bin/gbrain-serve-wrapper.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Kill ALL existing gbrain serve processes first
pkill -9 -f "bun run.*cli.ts serve" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 1

# Verify no stale processes remain
if pgrep -f "bun run.*cli.ts serve" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: Failed to kill existing serve processes"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Starting fresh gbrain serve..."
cd ~/gbrain && exec bun run src/cli.ts serve
```

This ensures every MCP spawn starts with a clean slate, avoiding the lock contention issue.

- Only one healthy serve process runs at a time
- CLI sync operations work reliably

## Workaround Attempted — Singleton Wrapper Fails in OpenClaw MCP

I tried implementing the singleton wrapper approach suggested in the issue. Here is what happened:

### What I tried
Created a bash wrapper script (`gbrain-singleton.sh`) that:
1. Detects stale gbrain serve processes (stdin=/dev/null or PPID=1)
2. Kills them before spawning a new one
3. Cleans up stale lock files

### Why it fails in OpenClaw
The singleton approach requires `exec bun ...` to replace the shell with the gbrain serve process. In OpenClaw's MCP spawn model, this breaks the stdio pipe chain:

- OpenClaw spawns `bash -c "singleton.sh start"`
- The shell `exec`s into `bun run cli.ts serve`
- OpenClaw loses its reference to the stdio socket
- Result: `Error: MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms`

The old serve process (stdin=/dev/null) never gets cleaned up because OpenClaw never sees it as a child it manages.

### Root Cause (reiterated)
OpenClaw's MCP lifecycle:
1. Gateway restart → spawns new gbrain serve
2. Old serve's stdin redirected to /dev/null (orphaned)
3. Old serve still holds PGLite lock
4. New serve holds new lock → lock contention

### Suggested Fix Directions

**Option A — Shorter stale lock threshold**
The PGLite lock already has stale detection (5 min threshold), but it relies on `process.kill(pid, 0)` to check if alive. The stale cleanup only triggers when the next process tries to acquire the lock. If the stale threshold were shorter (e.g., 30 seconds instead of 5 minutes), deadlocks would resolve faster.

**Option B — serve process self-cleanup on startup**
Add an optional flag to `gbrain serve` that:
1. On startup, checks for any existing gbrain serve processes
2. Validates whether the other process is responsive (not stdin=/dev/null and not orphaned)
3. If unresponsive, kills it before acquiring the lock

**Option C — OpenClaw MCP fix**
Properly clean up MCP server processes before restart. This is the most correct fix but requires upstream OpenClaw changes.

### Current Status
- gbrain: latest (v0.21.0)
- OpenClaw: v2026.4.22
- MCP config reverted to direct `bun run ... serve`
- Lock contention still reproduced after each gateway restart

The issue is real and the workaround suggested in the issue does not work in OpenClaw's MCP spawn model. Would appreciate guidance on which fix direction would be accepted.

**Root Cause Identified & Fixed ✅**

**Issue:** PGLite WASM initialization failure with `PGLite failed to initialize its WASM runtime. Aborted()`

**Root Cause:** The file `/root/brain/postmaster.pid` was stale. The process with PID listed in the file had already terminated, but PGLite checks this file at startup and aborts if it believes another instance is already running.

Hi @Aragorn2046 — I hit the same bug class independently while working on a project that drives `gbrain serve` from a long-running Python daemon. I'd built a patch with the same goal as #591 by the time I noticed your PR, so this comment is partly a "ack, you got there first," partly an offer to fold our extra coverage into yours if it's useful.

Our patch (rebased on top of `9c2dc4c` / v0.26.8, sits cleanly with #591's HTTP-path changes since we're stdio-only) shares the three core ideas with yours:

- **POSIX signals** — SIGINT / SIGTERM / **SIGHUP**.
- **stdin lifecycle** — both `'end'` and `'close'`.
- **Parent watchdog** — 5s polling, gated on `initialParentPid !== 1`.

A few additions on top, plus one finding that affects #591 directly:

### 1. The `process.ppid` watchdog never fires on Bun (macOS, likely Linux too)

Both Node and Bun expose `process.ppid` as a property captured at process creation; it does **not** refresh when the kernel re-parents the child to PID 1. I built a small repro to confirm — outer Python parent SIGKILLs itself; the kernel re-parents the bun child within one second (`ps -o ppid= -p <child>` returns `1`), but inside the child `process.ppid` stays at the original parent ID indefinitely.

```
startup process.ppid=87589
tick process.ppid=87589 live(ps)=87589
tick process.ppid=87589 live(ps)=1     ← kernel re-parented; process.ppid did NOT update
tick process.ppid=87589 live(ps)=1
tick process.ppid=87589 live(ps)=1
```

So the watchdog at #591's [serve.ts:60](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/591/files) (`if (initialParentPid !== 1 && process.ppid === 1)`) won't actually trip in a real launchd / cron / orphaned-PPID scenario. The fix is one helper that goes through `spawnSync('ps', ['-o', 'ppid=', '-p', $$])` instead — ~10ms per 5s tick, falls back to `process.ppid` if `ps` is unavailable.

This is the one finding I'd flag as actionable for #591 as-is, regardless of whether you fold in the rest of our work.

### 2. Other additions in our patch

- **`engine.disconnect()` cleanup deadline** — 5s race; if disconnect wedges (PGLite WASM stall or similar), `process.exit(0)` still runs. The orphaned lock dir is then reclaimed on the next attempt by the existing stale-lock check in `pglite-lock.ts`.
- **Optional `--stdio-idle-timeout <sec>`** — opt-in safety net (default OFF). Strict parsing (rejects `30junk` / `1.5` / `''` / missing) so a typo doesn't silently disable it. Also closes #446's feature request.
- **`!isTTY` gate on the stdin watchers** — interactive `gbrain serve` in a terminal won't shut down just because the user hasn't typed; signals + watchdog still cover them.
- **20 unit tests** with injectable `ServeOptions` seams (`stdin / signals / exit / log / startMcpServer / getParentPid / setInterval / clearInterval`) so the whole lifecycle is testable without a real Bun child or a real MCP SDK boot.

### 3. End-to-end repro evidence

A bash + Python harness drives 4 disconnect cases against two builds (baseline = upstream master `9c2dc4c`, patched = our branch). Per the design we adopted, child liveness + the lock dir's PID JSON + `kill -0` are primary evidence; `gbrain stats` latency is secondary. The lock state is captured BEFORE running stats so `stats` can't self-heal a stale dir and skew the snapshot.

| case | side | child PID | lock state (pre-stats) | `stats` (latency) | lifecycle reason |
|------|------|-----------|------------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| stdin-close | baseline | alive | live-lock pid=88224 | timeout-8s (8s) | (none) |
| stdin-close | patched | alive | no-lock-dir | ok (0s) | graceful exit (stdin-end) |
| sigterm | baseline | alive | live-lock pid=88331 | timeout-8s (8s) | (none) |
| sigterm | patched | alive | no-lock-dir | ok (0s) | graceful exit (SIGTERM) |
| sigkill-parent | baseline | dead | stale-lock pid=88415 | ok (0s) | (none) |
| sigkill-parent | patched | dead | no-lock-dir | ok (1s) | graceful exit (stdin-end) |
| watchdog-fifo | baseline | alive | live-lock pid=88573 | timeout-8s (8s) | (none) |
| watchdog-fifo | patched | dead | no-lock-dir | ok (1s) | graceful exit (parent-died) |

`watchdog-fifo` is the launchd / orphan case — child's stdin is held open by an external keeper (named FIFO) so the patch can't fall through to stdin EOF; only the watchdog can detect parent death. Without the `process.ppid` → `spawnSync('ps')` fix, this row matched `live-lock pid=…` on patched too.

Repro harness: see `parent.py` and `run.sh` linked in the branch below. macOS / Bun 1.3.12. Maintainer can re-run with `bun install --frozen-lockfile && /tmp/gbrain-repro/run.sh`.

### 4. Background

Reproduction surfaced this on our side: a long-running parent (`gbrain_sync_daemon.py`) spawns `gbrain serve --stdio` as an MCP child. When the parent times out the child via `proc.terminate()`, the gbrain process used to live on as a PPID=1 orphan holding the PGLite lock; subsequent sync ticks all failed with `Timed out waiting for PGLite lock` until the 5-min stale check kicked in. With this patch the child exits within ~5s of the parent dying via every observed code path.

### Proposed paths from here

- **(A)** I push my branch and you cherry-pick / squash whatever you want onto this PR. You stay the listed author. Easiest if you want to keep momentum on #591.
- **(B)** I open a separate PR superseding #591 with everything integrated, `Related to #591` in the body and full credit to your three features (SIGHUP / stdin close / watchdog) in the commit. We'd close #591 once the new PR lands.
- **(C)** Cherry-pick **only** the `process.ppid` → `spawnSync('ps')` fix to #591 and leave the rest as a follow-up PR.

Stale-ppid bug confirmed on Bun 1.3.11 macOS arm64. Repro: Python parent spawns Bun child, parent SIGKILL's itself, kernel reparents Bun child to PID 1 (launchd) — but `process.ppid` inside Bun stays frozen at the dead parent's PID for the entire process lifetime.

**ps after parent death:** PPID=1 (correct)  
**Bun process.ppid:** original parent PID (stale, never updates)  
**Node.js same scenario:** PPID correctly updates to 1 from first tick

Root cause: Bun likely caches `ppid` at startup rather than calling `getppid()` on each access.

Watchdog gating in `serve.ts:60` (`process.ppid !== 1`) will need a fallback path until upstream lands. Workaround: shell out to `ps -o ppid= -p $$` on each watchdog check.

Confirmed on **v0.27.0** (Postgres engine, macOS arm64). The same structural CLI-dispatch bug also affects `gbrain init --help`, with **higher blast radius** than `sync --help` because `init` *overwrites `~/.gbrain/config.json`*.

## Repro

```bash
# Existing postgres brain configured by /setup-gbrain
$ cat ~/.gbrain/config.json
{ "engine": "postgres", "database_url": "postgresql://..." }

$ gbrain init --help

Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
  Schema version 1 → 36 (32 migration(s) pending)
  [2] slugify_existing_pages...

$ cat ~/.gbrain/config.json
{ "engine": "pglite", "database_path": "/Users/.../.gbrain/brain.pglite" }
# Postgres config silently replaced. Subsequent `gbrain stats` reports the empty PGLite brain.
```

## Impact

`init` is the most catastrophic command for the `--help` regression to fall through on:

- existing `config.json` is overwritten in place (engine=postgres → engine=pglite, `database_url` lost)
- previously-set `embedding_model` / `embedding_dimensions` are lost
- a brand-new PGLite brain is created at the default path

In `src/cli.ts`, the `CLI_ONLY` set should at minimum short-circuit on `--help` / `-h` for **every** member, not just rely on each command implementing its own help printing. `init`'s case in particular should be hardened with the explicit guard:

```ts
case 'init': {
  if (args.includes('--help') || args.includes('-h')) {
    printInitHelp();
    return;
  }
  ...
}
```

The full CLI-wide pattern proposed in #578 would also work; flagging this so the fix scope explicitly includes `init` (and the destructive overwrite path).

**Confirming repro on v0.30.0** — same `unknown_transport` over stdio MCP, with the diagnosis in OP still accurate. Adding context that may help disambiguate the fix.

## v0.30.0 codebase observation

In current `src/mcp/server.ts:30-42`, the stdio dispatch deliberately sets `remote: true` (not `false` as OP's grep on v0.28.6 suggested):

```ts
return dispatchToolCall(engine, name, params, {
  remote: true,
  takesHoldersAllowList: ['world'],
});
```

Per the in-line comment, this is **intentional** — it limits what `takes_list`, `takes_search`, and `query` expose to a stdio agent caller (private hunches stay private; only `world`-holder takes leak through). Flipping stdio to `remote: false` would regress the v0.28 takes-protection contract.

## Why only `whoami` mis-detects

The `remote: true` + `!ctx.auth` combination is unambiguous for every other operation: dispatch routes them through the takes-holder allow-list and they return correct (filtered) results. **Only `whoami` (`src/core/operations.ts:2031-2046`) treats this combination as a "transport bug" and fail-closes.**

But `(remote: true, auth: undefined)` over stdio isn't a bug — it's the *defined* shape of the trusted-local-pipe-without-per-token-auth surface, distinct from HTTP-without-auth (which genuinely is a bug).

## Suggested fix shape (without touching trust boundary)

Either:

**(a) Add `ctx.transport: 'stdio' | 'http'`** threaded from the entry points. `whoami` returns `transport: 'local'` when `transport === 'stdio'` regardless of auth presence. Cleanest separation.

**(b) Treat `(ctx.remote === true && !ctx.auth)` as `transport: 'local', scopes: []`** in `whoami` only. Stays one-line. The fail-closed posture for HTTP-without-auth still triggers via the HTTP transport's own auth middleware before reaching dispatch.

Option (b) is minimal and keeps the v0.26.9 trust-boundary intact for everywhere except `whoami`'s introspection — which is what users actually want from a stdio caller anyway.

Happy to PR (b) if you confirm direction. Tested on Claude Code stdio MCP integration; all 30+ other tools (`query`, `get_stats`, `get_health`, `list_pages`, etc.) work flawlessly over the same transport.

Hitting this from a different angle that's worth flagging for prioritization: **#428 makes gbrain v0.30.x's worktree-aware source IDs functionally a no-op.**

gbrain v0.30 (PR #730+) introduced path-hash source IDs (`<slug>-<pathhash8>`) so Conductor sibling worktrees of the same repo can each have their own indexed code source — the headline win was "semantic results match the actual code on disk in this worktree, not whichever sibling synced last." gstack v1.29.0.0 (PR garrytan/gstack#1382) wired this up via `gbrain sources add` + `gbrain sources attach` + a `.gbrain-source` pin file in the worktree root.

That part works. The pin file is written, `gbrain sources list` shows the path-hash source, capability checks pass.

But this bug means the pin's target source stays at `page_count=0` forever, because every write path I tried lands in `default`:

**Repro on a freshly registered worktree-scoped source:**

```bash
# Source registered + pin written by gstack v1.29.0.0
gbrain sources list --json | jq '.sources[] | select(.id | startswith("gstack-code-cher"))'
# → { "id": "gstack-code-cher-f0a8ea3a-b719da", "local_path": "/home/alex/TMASearcher", "page_count": 0, ... }

# Try a direct write with --source
echo "test marker token_8a72" | gbrain put "_pin_test" --source gstack-code-cher-f0a8ea3a-b719da
gbrain search "token_8a72"
# → finds the page (good)

# But where did it land?
psql -c "SELECT source_id, COUNT(*) FROM pages GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC"
#  source_id                          | count
# ------------------------------------+-------
#  default                            |   165   ← +1 from the put
#  gstack-code-cher-f0a8ea3a-b719da   |     0   ← pin target, still empty
```

Same with the orchestrator's code stage: `gbrain sync --strategy code --source <id>` walks the repo, imports 30 files, and they all land in `default` because `performFullSync` calls `runImport(engine, importArgs)` without passing `sourceId` through (see `src/commands/sync.ts:889` calling `import.ts:runImport` — the latter has no `sourceId` parameter).

**Net effect:** the `.gbrain-source` pin routes *reads* correctly (federated query just falls through to `default` because the pin target is empty), but no `gbrain code-def`/`code-refs` ever returns hits scoped to the actual worktree, because the worktree-scoped source never accumulates pages. From the user's perspective, the v1.29.0.0 wave is invisible until #428 lands.

PR #774 adds `--src-subpath <subdir>` and `--exclude <glob>` to `gbrain sync`.

**`--src-subpath`**: scopes a sync to a subdirectory of the git repo — `gbrain sync --src-subpath wiki` walks only `wiki/`, keeps slugs as `wiki/page-name` (git-root-relative), runs all git ops against the repo root. **`--exclude <glob>`**: repeatable flag, works in both full and incremental sync paths.

**Follow-up commit: `b4bfb70`** — `fix(sync): gate slugRoot on opts.srcSubpath`

Discovered during live testing: the original PR applied `slugRoot = gitContextRoot` whenever `syncScopeRoot !== gitContextRoot`, which affected **all** subdirectory sources — not just `--src-subpath` cases. Sources registered with a direct subdirectory path (e.g., `sources add wiki --path ~/atlas/shared/wiki`) carry `slug:` frontmatter fields matching their path-relative slug (`agent-roster`, not `shared/wiki/agent-roster`). The mismatch caused 80/144 wiki pages to fail import with `SLUG_MISMATCH`.

Fix: `slugRoot = (opts.srcSubpath && scopeRel) ? gitContextRoot : undefined`

Git-root-relative slugs are only activated when `--src-subpath` is **explicitly passed**. Back-compat with existing sources that point directly at subdirectories is preserved.

I can reproduce the same class of issue on current `master` / `gbrain 0.30.2` with an OpenAI-compatible local embedding endpoint.

Environment:

- gbrain: `0.30.2` (`410c697` + local patch for testing)
- DB: local Postgres + pgvector
- embedding model: `ollama:Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ`
- provider base URL: local OpenAI-compatible server (`provider_base_urls.ollama = http://localhost:8000/v1`)
- `embedding_dimensions = 1536`

Observed before patch:

```text
Embedding dim mismatch: model Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ returned 2560 but schema expects 1536.
```

Root cause appears to be that `embedding_dimensions` is used to size/check the DB schema, but for `openai-compatible` providers it is only passed through for Voyage models via `output_dimension`. Models such as Qwen3 Embedding support Matryoshka-style truncation via an OpenAI-compatible `dimensions` request field, but gbrain does not currently send it.

A small local patch fixed it for us by adding a provider options branch roughly like:

```ts
if (/^Qwen3-Embedding/i.test(modelId)) {
  return { openaiCompatible: { dimensions: dims } };
}
```

After that, `gbrain put` succeeds and doctor reports:

```text
embedding_provider: ollama:Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ ✓ ..., 1536 dims, DB aligned
```

Suggestion: make `openai-compatible` embedding dimension passthrough configurable instead of hardcoding per model. For example:

```json
{
  "embedding_model": "ollama:Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ",
  "embedding_dimensions": 1536,
  "provider_base_urls": { "ollama": "http://localhost:8000/v1" },
  "embedding_dimension_param": "dimensions"
}
```

or provider-scoped:

```json
{
  "provider_options": {
    "ollama": {
      "embedding_dimensions_field": "dimensions"
    }
  }
}
```

This would cover Qwen3 / local OpenAI-compatible servers without needing local source patches on every upgrade.

## Update — verified that this is independent of pooler routing

After enabling Supabase IPv4 add-on (so the direct port becomes reachable) and re-testing with `GBRAIN_DISABLE_DIRECT_POOL` unset and `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` pointed at the direct connection (port 5432), the error reproduces identically:

```
$ GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL="$SUPABASE_DB_DIRECT_URL" gbrain reindex-frontmatter --yes --force
UNSAFE_TRANSACTION: Only use sql.begin, sql.reserved or max: 1
```

So the title's framing ("incompatible with Supabase pooler transaction mode") is misleading. The real constraint is **postgres-js with `max: 1` refuses raw `BEGIN` calls regardless of port or transaction mode.** The Supabase pooler doesn't make it worse — it just made me notice it first because the pooler was the only working path until IPv4 was enabled.

Confirms the right upstream fix is workaround #2 from the issue (route through ConnectionManager / use `sql.begin()`), not workaround #3 (pooler-detection heuristic). The pooler isn't the discriminator — `max: 1` is.

Suggested retitle: "backfill-effective-date: raw BEGIN/COMMIT incompatible with postgres-js max:1 client config"

Root-caused this and bundled the fix into #768 so #767 + #769 ship together (they're complementary halves of the same code-ingest path — #767 makes chunks exist, #769 keeps their metadata alive).

**Root cause** (more precise than the original report's "extract / autopilot suspicion"):

`embed.ts` has three re-upsert call sites — `embedOnePage`, `embedAll` non-stale, `embedAllStale` (autopilot common path). All three load chunks via `getChunks()` (which DOES return the metadata) and then map them to a fresh `ChunkInput` with only 5 fields:

```ts
const updated: ChunkInput[] = chunks.map(c => ({
  chunk_index: c.chunk_index,
  chunk_text: c.chunk_text,
  chunk_source: c.chunk_source,
  embedding: embeddingMap.get(c.chunk_index),
  token_count: c.token_count || Math.ceil(c.chunk_text.length / 4),
}));
```

The 8 metadata fields (`language`, `symbol_name`, `symbol_type`, `start_line`, `end_line`, `parent_symbol_path`, `doc_comment`, `symbol_name_qualified`) get dropped. Then `upsertChunks`'s ON CONFLICT clause overwrites them from `EXCLUDED` unconditionally — the asymmetric outlier vs `embedding`/`embedded_at`/`model`/`embedding_image`, which already use a chunk_text-gated CASE pattern. So every embed pass nukes them to NULL.

Not the chunker, not extract, not autopilot rewrites — the embed path itself.

**Fix in #768** (commit `2be8040`):
1. New `preserveCodeMetadata(loaded, base)` helper threading metadata through all three re-upsert sites in `embed.ts`.
2. Defense-in-depth: applied the chunk_text-gated CASE pattern to all 8 metadata columns in both `postgres-engine.ts` and `pglite-engine.ts` `upsertChunks`. Symmetric with the embedding column's existing pattern.
3. Three regression tests in `test/embed.serial.test.ts` covering `--stale` / `--all` / `--slugs`. Each fails on pre-fix code (8 fields come back undefined) and passes on the patched code.

**Backfill needed after deploy**: `gbrain sync --strategy code --force --source <id>` per code source, since re-embed alone never produces metadata — only the chunker does. Existing NULL chunks stay NULL until re-chunked.

Repo I confirmed on: 4875 code pages × ~10 chunks/page on a real gbrain DB, all NULL metadata. `code-def` returned 0 hits for every nvr/cloudapi/dragon symbol I tried.
Closing this PR; withdrawing the contribution.

For context: this fix is the surgical entry point to a broader OAuth-auth-broken cluster of community reports. The full family:

- #803 — confidential-client auth-code flow broken (SDK clientAuth plaintext vs hashed `client_secret`)
- #781 — same root cause, phrased as "getClient returns hash where SDK expects plaintext"
- #720 — DCR + auth-code: every `/token` returns `invalid_client`

This PR specifically unblocks the **PKCE-only (`token_endpoint_auth_method=none`) Claude Desktop confidential-client OAuth flow**, which is one slice of the cluster — the slice where the OAuth spec says "no secret should be required" but the SDK rejects on the truthy stored hash. Returning `undefined` for that case is the spec-clean fix and is independent of the larger plaintext-vs-hash question in #803/#781/#720.

The DB still stores the hash, so a client switching auth methods later is unaffected. Verified against `gbrain serve --http` on v0.31.10 with Claude Desktop's OAuth flow.

Happy to follow up with a separate PR for the confidential-client (#803) path if useful — that one needs more design discussion (do you want the SDK to see the hash and gbrain to hash-compare in middleware, or have getClient return plaintext from a separate column?).

Adding a concrete Hermes/Codex repro for this.

## Repro from Hermes-backed setup

Environment:
- Brain repo: `/Users/barron/Developer/wiki`
- Transcript corpus: exported Hermes sessions as `.txt` files under `/Users/barron/.gbrain/transcripts/hermes-sessions`
- Hermes already has working LLM auth via `openai-codex` / Codex OAuth and can run agent jobs normally.
- No direct `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is present in the GBrain process environment.

Commands:

```bash
cd /Users/barron/Developer/wiki
gbrain config set dream.synthesize.session_corpus_dir /Users/barron/.gbrain/transcripts/hermes-sessions
gbrain config set dream.synthesize.enabled true
gbrain dream --dry-run --json
```

Observed:

```text
synthesize: dry-run: 0 of 557 transcripts would synthesize
reason: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for significance judge
```

The pipeline is otherwise wired correctly: Hermes sessions export successfully, GBrain discovers 557 transcripts, but synthesis cannot even run the significance filter because `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` constructs an Anthropic client directly via `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead of using the configured/available agent LLM route.

## Expected behavior

Dream synthesis should use the same provider/auth abstraction as the rest of the agent environment, or at least support a configurable fallback. In a Hermes deployment, that likely means one of:

- inherit/use Hermes' active provider/auth route, e.g. `openai-codex` / Codex OAuth;
- use a configured local helper command that shells out to Hermes/Codex and returns a `messages.create`-compatible response;
- or route through GBrain's existing model/provider config rather than hard-failing when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is absent.

Direct Anthropic should remain a supported fast path, but it should not be required for dreaming when another working authenticated LLM route exists.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- `gbrain dream --phase synthesize --dry-run --json` can judge transcript significance without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when an alternate configured provider/helper is available.
- Full `gbrain dream --json` can run synthesize/subagent workers through that same provider/helper path.
- The report should distinguish “no LLM route configured” from “Anthropic key absent.”
- Long transcript prompts should use stdin or prompt files rather than fragile argv-sized prompt strings if the fallback is command-based.

**Follow-up: how connected agents actually route to the brain — surfacing two implications that affect the RFC.**

When we sat with "drop the URL into Claude Desktop / openclaw / Hermes, get memory tools," we realized we'd glossed over a real split on the agent side. Two archetypes:

| Archetype | Examples | How it knows when to use the brain | What gets "installed" |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tool-description-driven** | Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Perplexity | Reads `tools/list` from MCP; each tool's `description` + JSON schema teaches the agent when to call it. | Nothing. Paste URL + token into the client's MCP config. |
| **Skill-driven** | openclaw (today), future Hermes | Reads markdown skill files at boot. Skills give the agent procedural instructions: *"on any inbound, check the brain first; route X to `intake`, route Y to `search`."* | Skills + an `AGENTS.md` pointer. Today baked into the runtime image at `/opt/gbrain/skills/*`. |

These coexist. They're not substitutes.

**Implication 1 — the description-quality bar on `operations.ts` is one of the deliverables.**

For tool-description-driven agents, the *entire* "when should I use this tool, what do the return values mean, how do I choose between `intake` and `put_page` if both are exposed" burden is carried by the tool's `description` + JSON schema. The skill-driven agents have markdown to lean on; Claude Desktop has the tool descriptions and nothing else.

This means: even if we agree on the three-plane cut + add `intake`, the *prose* in each operation's description is load-bearing for half the audience. Sloppy descriptions = Claude Desktop misuses the tools. Worth treating description quality as a first-class concern of the RFC, not an afterthought.

**Implication 2 — an open question worth your take.**

Right now skill-driven agents (openclaw today) bake skills into the runtime image. That works but it's a tight coupling: rolling a new skill means rolling a new image. Alternative: **the brain stores its own skills as memory** (`brain/skills/*.md`), and skill-driven agents discover them via `list_pages(folder: "skills/")` at boot.

Pros:
- Single source of truth. The brain teaches its own consumers.
- Skill iteration without image rebuilds. A team can write a custom skill into their brain that openclaw picks up on next restart.
- Brain content + brain instructions live together, version-controlled together (since gbrain's brain repo is git-backed).

Cons:
- Bootstrap chicken-and-egg: the agent has to know to `list_pages(folder: "skills/")` *before* it has any skills telling it what to do. Solvable with a minimum hard-coded "fetch skills, then read them" boot sequence — but that minimum bootstrap is itself a tiny baked-in skill.
- Cross-brain shared skills (the ones every brain should have) might want a different distribution channel than per-brain custom skills.

**Not asking for this to be part of the RFC outcome** — flagging because:
1. It sits at the same seam as the data/control split (skills are control-plane, but if they live in the brain they're stored as memory). The cut may inform itself.
2. If your model is "skills are always image-side / external to the brain," that's a real position and we'll defer to it.
3. If your model is "skills could be brain-resident," that changes how `operations.ts` should expose skill management — and would be worth surfacing in the same audit.

So: same redirect-or-affirm posture as the parent RFC. Not asking you to design this; just flagging it so the original RFC isn't missing a load-bearing concern.

Multi-agent OpenClaw setup here, Czech exam-prep coaching agents bound to Telegram group topics, gbrain holding the syllabus corpus (Postgres + Supabase backend, v0.33.0). Trying to combine Active Memory + gbrain hits two concrete walls:

**1. **2. Different problems.** The merged `gbrain-context` engine (v0.32.5, #880) solves *state* injection (time/location/calendar/tasks). | `exam-prep-kacka` | **23** | 14× `gbrain__query`, 8× `gbrain__search`, 1× `gbrain__resolve_slugs` |

Update after reproducing and validating a deploy fix:

The original `ingest_log.source_id` failure is one instance of a broader ordering problem in `PostgresEngine.applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` vs `SCHEMA_SQL` replay.

On an existing Railway Postgres database, upgrading to `v0.35.0.0` (`baf1a47798cb145d00bfce4fa94f85a94c8d7e07`) still failed after working around `idx_ingest_log_source_type_created`. The next failure was:

```text
column "federated_read" does not exist
[bootstrap] ERROR: Command '['gbrain', 'init', '--migrate-only']' returned non-zero exit status 1.
```

Root cause appears to be that v0.35 fresh schema adds indexes over new OAuth source-scope columns before older databases have those columns:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_oauth_clients_source_id
  ON oauth_clients(source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_oauth_clients_federated_read
  ON oauth_clients USING GIN (federated_read);
```

But the v0.35 migration registry still only runs through `v0_32_2`; newer fresh-schema columns rely on `verifySchema()` after schema replay. That is too late for indexed columns, because `conn.unsafe(sqlText)` fails first.

A narrow fix that worked in production was to add `oauth_clients.source_id` and `oauth_clients.federated_read` to the Postgres forward-reference bootstrap, just like the existing `ingest_log.source_id` bootstrap path:

```ts
const needsOauthClientsScope = probe.oauth_clients_exists
  && (!probe.oauth_clients_source_id_exists || !probe.oauth_clients_federated_read_exists);

if (needsOauthClientsScope) {
  await conn.unsafe(`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sources (
      id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      name          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      local_path    TEXT,
      last_commit   TEXT,
      last_sync_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
      config        JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
      created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    INSERT INTO sources (id, name, config)
      VALUES ('default', 'default', '{"federated": true}'::jsonb)
      ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;
    ALTER TABLE oauth_clients ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT
      REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
    ALTER TABLE oauth_clients ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS federated_read TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';
  `);
}
```

Validation from the downstream Railway wrapper:

- rebuilt with GBrain `v0.35.0.0` / `baf1a47798cb145d00bfce4fa94f85a94c8d7e07`
- applied the above patch during image build
- `gbrain init --migrate-only` completed
- runtime started `GBrain MCP Server v0.35.0.0`
- Railway `/ready` returned `200 OK`
- filtered logs no longer show `source_id does not exist` or `federated_read does not exist`

This suggests the upstream fix should be in `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` rather than deleting index statements from `schema.sql`.

For others landing here while #429 awaits upstream wiring, here's the minimum reproducible setup that worked for me on a thin-client install (Mac CLI → MCP → Railway-hosted `gbrain serve --http` → Supabase):

**`~/.gbrain/hooks/signal-capture.sh`** (mode 755):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail
trap 'exit 0' ERR
PAYLOAD=$(cat 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')
PROMPT=$(echo "$PAYLOAD" | jq -r '.prompt // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
[ -z "$PROMPT" ] && exit 0
NORM=$(echo "$PROMPT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -d '[:punct:]' | xargs)
case "$NORM" in ok|si|no|sigue|continue|thanks|done|"") exit 0 ;; esac
[ "${#PROMPT}" -lt 10 ] && exit 0
cat <<'EOF'
[hook: signal-capture] If this message contains substantive content (original thinking, entity mentions, decisions, pending actions), invoke the signal-detector skill via the Skill tool before responding. Spawn as background Agent so it does not block. Skip silently for operational messages.
EOF
exit 0
```

**`~/.claude/settings.json` addition:**
```json
"hooks": {
  "UserPromptSubmit": [{
    "hooks": [{
      "type": "command",
      "command": "/Users/<you>/.gbrain/hooks/signal-capture.sh",
      "timeout": 10
    }]
  }]
}
```

Pattern follows Anthropic's UserPromptSubmit doctrine at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (synchronous, <30s, stdout injected as context, exit 0 fail-open). It is a reminder injector — Claude still has to obey the injected context. But the reminder fires on EVERY message, which is the missing piece. Compliance went from ~0% to ~near 100% in my sessions after wiring this.

## Update: root cause is different from what I filed

After further investigation the real failure path is:

1. `bun` auto-loads `.env` from CWD into `process.env` on every CLI execution.
2. Project `.env` files (e.g. Docker stacks, mono-repos) commonly contain a `DATABASE_URL` intended for a sibling service (here: a Postgres container inside Docker, unreachable from the host).
3. gbrain's `loadConfig` (`src/core/config.ts:143-145`) sees `DATABASE_URL` in env and promotes inferred engine to `postgres` **regardless of `~/.gbrain/config.json` having `engine: pglite`**.
4. PostgresEngine then attempts to connect to the bogus URL → `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`.

The `[WARN] connection: Could not connect to configured DB (URL from env:DATABASE_URL)` message in doctor IS truthful — I'd dismissed it as upstream-buggy because I'd checked the shell with `bash -c 'echo "${DATABASE_URL:+set}"'` and seen unset. But `gbrain` is bun-executed and bun re-loads `.env` from CWD; the shell scope wasn't the right place to look.

## Verified fix from user side

Running `cd /tmp && gbrain apply-migrations --yes` unwedged all 15 queued migrations cleanly through to v0.32.2.

## Suggested upstream fix

The current inference (`src/core/config.ts:143-145`):
```ts
const inferredEngine: 'postgres' | 'pglite' = dbUrl
    ? 'postgres'
    : fileConfig?.engine || (fileConfig?.database_path ? 'pglite' : 'postgres');
```

Rule of least surprise: an explicit `~/.gbrain/config.json` with `engine: pglite` should win over an ambient `DATABASE_URL` from the CWD's bun-auto-loaded `.env`. The current ordering makes a sibling service's env var silently hijack engine selection. Suggested:

```ts
// Explicit config-file engine selection wins over ambient env URL.
// Env URL still wins when fileConfig is absent OR when fileConfig declares engine=postgres.
const inferredEngine: 'postgres' | 'pglite' =
    fileConfig?.engine === 'pglite' ? 'pglite' :
    dbUrl ? 'postgres' :
    fileConfig?.engine || (fileConfig?.database_path ? 'pglite' : 'postgres');
```

At minimum the failure message would benefit from naming `bun`'s `.env` auto-load as a likely source ("DATABASE_URL is set in `process.env` — if you didn't set it intentionally, check for a `.env` file in the directory you're running gbrain from").

Apologies for the noise on the original filing. The reproduction recipe was correct *as a symptom*, but the suggested fix was wrong because I'd misidentified the proximate cause. Happy to close this and re-file as a narrower issue if you'd prefer.

After running this through `/plan-eng-review` and `/codex` (outside-voice adversarial review), we integrated it on top of master in #1129 with some refactoring. Summary of what changed and why:

**Three correctness fixes codex caught:**

1. **Cache contamination via `knobsHash()`.** Without bumping `KNOBS_HASH_VERSION` 2→3 in `src/core/search/mode.ts`, a cached no-floor result gets served to a floor-enabled call. Same bug class CDX-4 v0.32.3 hotfix closed for the other search-lite knobs. Direct ranking-correctness leak — the PR would have shipped with this.
2. **NaN scores bypass the gate.** `NaN < threshold` is false in JS, so a NaN-scored row would have skipped the floor and received boosts. Realistic on Voyage flexible-dim or zembed-1 Matryoshka dim drift across reindexes. Fixed: NaN scores skip the boost entirely.
3. **Negative top scores break "single result trivially eligible".** Your single-result test passed because score was positive; with a negative top score (-0.5), threshold becomes -0.425 and the top itself fails its own floor. Edge case but real on RRF outputs that can go negative.

**Two architectural shape changes:**

- **Single up-front threshold vs per-stage recompute.** Your PR computes the threshold separately at each stage (each of backlink → salience → recency uses `topScore × ratio` from the array state at that moment). Codex argued this makes stage order part of the API — a backlink boost to the leader raises the salience/recency floor and gates out a page that was originally within `0.85 × top`. We refactored to compute the threshold ONCE at `runPostFusionStages` entry from the post-cosine-rescore snapshot, then pass the same number to all three stages. Order-independent.
- **Public surface beyond `PostFusionOpts`.** Wired `SearchOpts.floorRatio` (per-call), `search.floor_ratio` config key (operator default — included in `SEARCH_MODE_CONFIG_KEYS`), and a `floor_ratio` field on `MODE_BUNDLES` (currently `undefined` for all three modes pending gbrain-side ablation). No `GBRAIN_SEARCH_FLOOR_RATIO` env var — `resolveSearchMode()` is pure by design, and a hidden env knob would make `gbrain search modes` lie about the resolved state.

**API surface change:** the three boost functions now take `floorThreshold?: number` (an absolute score floor) instead of `floorRatio?: number`. `runPostFusionStages` is the single ratio→threshold converter. This is what makes the single-baseline semantic enforceable through the type system. Your tests' shape stays similar; they update from passing `0.85` to passing `0.85 * topScore` inline.

**What stays exactly as you shipped:**

- Default-off posture is correct and preserved.
- Empirical framing (dense-embedder targeting, `0.85` starting value, leapfrog regression mechanism) is unchanged — your ablation is what motivates the whole thing.
- Gate scope (metadata-axis boost stages only, exact-match runs independently) matches your design intent.

\`\`\`sql
WITH unambiguous AS (
  SELECT p.id, MAX(m.source_id) AS target
  FROM pages p
  JOIN _source_file_map m ON p.frontmatter->>'file' = m.file_path
  WHERE p.source_id = 'default' AND p.type = 'code'
  GROUP BY p.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m.source_id) = 1
)
UPDATE pages SET source_id = u.target FROM unambiguous u WHERE pages.id = u.id;
\`\`\`

Reproduced on Linux with v0.35.1.1, with a different CPU profile that may help narrow this down.

### Environment

- **gbrain version**: 0.35.1.1
- **OS**: Linux 6.8.0 (Ubuntu, x86_64)
- **Backend**: PGLite (`~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`)
- **Embedding provider**: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dims)
- **Host**: OpenClaw 2026.5.12 — keeps `gbrain serve` (from the bundled openclaw plugin) running continuously as an MCP subprocess. This is the architectural setup #677 describes.

### Reproduction

1. Run `gbrain dream --dry-run --json --dir <repo>` → completes in ~2.2s, reports `pages_synced: 107 (would)`, `lint_fixes: 7 (would)`, `embed: 1 chunk would be embedded`, no phase fails.
2. Run `gbrain dream --json --dir <repo>` (same dir, no `--dry-run`) → hangs.
3. Repeated against a smaller `--dir` scope (only 20 .md files) — **same hang**, so this is not workspace-content-specific.
4. Repeated isolating phases: `gbrain dream --phase lint --dir <repo>` — **also hangs**. The embed phase isn't reached; the hang starts earlier.

### What's different from the original report

The original report describes the hang as a deadlock with no CPU activity (no HTTP requests, no output). What I observe is **100% CPU on a single thread, no I/O wait**:

\`\`\`
$ ps -o pid,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,stat,cmd -p <pid>
    PID     ELAPSED %CPU %MEM    RSS STAT CMD
1550778       38:21  100  4.0 320484 Rl   bun .../gbrain dream --json --dir ...
$ cat /proc/<pid>/status | grep State
State:	R (running)
\`\`\`

This is a busy loop in JS/Bun, not an awaited promise that never resolves. Plausible interpretation: the lock acquisition path (probably contending with the openclaw-launched \`gbrain serve\` MCP subprocess per #677) retries in a tight loop without yielding or backoff, which would explain both the silent hang AND the CPU pattern. Could not confirm with a profiler in the moment, but the syscall pattern from a quick \`strace -p\` showed essentially no syscalls — pure userspace work.

### Stale lock on SIGKILL

When the hung process is \`SIGKILL\`'d (\`SIGTERM\` did not work; the busy loop didn't service it), the PGLite lock directory survives:

\`\`\`
/home/<user>/.gbrain/brain.pglite/.gbrain-lock/lock
\`\`\`

This persists indefinitely until manually removed (\`rm -rf .gbrain-lock/\`), at which point fresh \`gbrain\` invocations can proceed. Closed issue #251 covered the macOS variant of this; the cleanup gap also exists on Linux for SIGKILL paths.

### Concrete failure surface that motivated this

We had \`gbrain dream --json --dir <workspace>\` wired into an \`openclaw cron\` job (nightly). The cron's 1200s timeout fired, but it only killed the agent session that invoked \`exec\`. The spawned \`bun gbrain dream\` child survived as a 100%-CPU orphan, holding the PGLite lock, blocking every subsequent gbrain CLI invocation. Until that orphan is found and \`kill -9\`'d, the brain is effectively read-only.

So this hits cron-driven setups particularly hard: the orphan keeps the lock indefinitely AND consumes a full CPU until manually noticed.

Happy to bisect further (\`--phase backlinks\`, \`--phase sync\`, etc.) and report which is the earliest phase that hangs, if useful. Also happy to capture a \`py-spy\`/\`bun --inspect\` trace of the busy loop next time it reproduces.

In fact, I don't understand why are we enforcing a specific provider for anything. I understand setting defaults and even recommended providers. But what happens when a better or cheaper provider is available?

Pre-investigation completed as part of the v0.36.x fix-wave. The SDK's `authenticateClient` middleware (`node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/server/auth/middleware/clientAuth.js:23`) does `client.client_secret !== client_secret` — a plaintext compare against whatever `getClient()` returns. Our provider stores the hash at rest (correct security posture) so the SDK's plaintext compare always fails.

There is NO clean override seam in the current SDK — `authenticateClient` is imported and used directly by the SDK's `router.js`; we'd have to monkey-patch the imported binding to interpose.

Proper fix (deferred to a dedicated PR — out of scope for this wave's commit ordering):

1. Write our own `/token` endpoint that handles `client_secret_basic` / `client_secret_post` verification with bcrypt against `oauth_clients.client_secret_hash`.
2. Route the request to our `exchangeAuthorizationCode` / `exchangeRefreshToken` after verification.
3. Bypass `mcpAuthRouter` for /token only; keep it for /authorize + /register + /revoke.

Validated end-to-end against a real failing payload from an in-cluster litellm proxy fronting OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large`. Adding a follow-up commit ([f8319c4](https://github.com/Blockcast/gbrain/commit/f8319c4)) that you should review alongside the initial commit — the original PR had a regex gap I found during validation.

### Repro

`Blockcast/pim-multicast-gateway` checks in two vendored Sony chip-register `.h` files (`cxd2880-dvbt2_siena_mrc_a2.h`, 142 chunks, ~5664 chars/chunk; `cxd2880-dvb_siena_mrc_a2_br.h`, 113 chunks). Dense hex/binary register definitions pack ~1.5 chars/token under tiktoken vs the 4-char default. Estimated 200K tokens per page at 4 chars/token is comfortable; real token count is ~500K, well past OpenAI's 300K-per-request cap.

### Pre-fix state (master @ `1dadd9e`, no `LITELLM_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS`)

\`\`\`
gstack-code-pim-cluster | missing=255 | total=13255 | pct=1.92
\`\`\`

Both pages had 0/142 and 0/113 chunks embedded — the entire page's chunks were skipped after one rejected `embedMany` call. `gbrain sync` reported \"ok\" and the failures were invisible to the operator.

### Post-fix state (this PR @ `f8319c4`, `LITELLM_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=300000`)

\`\`\`
All 7 sources: missing=0
embed-stale job log: \"Embedded 255 chunks across 2 pages\"
\`\`\`

### The regex gap

The original commit (`738e1ad`) added the cap + env override but the safety-net recursion stayed dormant because `isTokenLimitError` didn't match the format litellm actually returns:

\`\`\`
litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': \"Invalid 'input': maximum request size is 300000 tokens per request.\"}}
\`\`\`

The existing regexes target Voyage-style messages (`max allowed tokens per submitted batch`, `batch contains too many tokens`, `token limit exceeded`). The OpenAI/litellm phrasing — `maximum request size is N tokens per request` — doesn't match any of them. `f8319c4` adds two regex branches for this variant + a unit test using the actual error string.

This is the variant most users will hit, since the pre-split is by tiktoken estimate and dense tokenized content (hex/binary tables, CJK, code with long identifiers) routinely exceeds the per-text estimate.

### Tests

\`\`\`
bun run typecheck — clean
test/ai/adaptive-embed-batch.test.ts — 33 pass / 0 fail
test/ai/ (whole dir) — 212 pass / 0 fail
\`\`\`

## v0.35.7.0 reproduced exactly what SunOpt + the follow-up commenter described

```
$ time gbrain query "投资" --expand false --limit 3
[0.87] daily/2026-02-09 -- ...
[0.84] daily/2026-05-17 -- ...
[0.53] daily/2026-02-09 -- ...
# (output complete here, but process does not exit)
```

- Hits stream out fine
- After the last hit, the bun process keeps running at **100% CPU on a single thread**
- RSS climbs steadily: 700MB → 1.0GB → 1.3GB inside one minute
- `strace -p <pid> -c` over 5 seconds shows **~16,000 `rt_sigreturn` syscalls** (≈3,200/sec) — pure userspace busy loop
- No HTTP requests reach LiteLLM (confirmed via `docker logs`), so it's not the LLM path
- SIGTERM ignored — only SIGKILL stops it (then the stale `.gbrain-lock/` survives, same as the follow-up comment noted)

This is the exact "fire-and-forget cache write keeping the bun event loop alive" signature: `void cache.store(...)` in `src/core/search/hybrid.ts` queues a PGLite write that the main path never awaits. On Postgres the write finishes in milliseconds and Bun exits cleanly; on PGLite (especially under 1024-dim DashScope vectors going through pgvector's HNSW path) the write takes long enough that Bun's event loop notices pending work and spins.

## v0.36.3.0 fixes it cleanly

Same query, same brain, same env, after `git pull && bun install && gbrain apply-migrations --yes`:

```
$ time gbrain query "投资" --expand false --limit 3
[0.87] daily/2026-02-09 -- ...
[0.84] daily/2026-05-17 -- ...
[0.53] daily/2026-02-09 -- ...

real    0m2.155s
user    0m2.230s
sys     0m0.408s
```

`pendingCacheWrites` + `awaitPendingSearchCacheWrites()` in v0.36.1.1's `hybrid.ts` is exactly the right fix — 19 lines that turn a fire-and-forget into a tracked Set the CLI drains before exit. Repeated runs show 1.9–2.2s, no zombie residue, no orphan `.gbrain-lock/`.

## Validates the bootstrap hypothesis in #1141's OP

The failure throws inside Phase A's `gbrain init --migrate-only` subprocess, before any v47+ migration runs. Source-text scan of v0.36.3.0 shows `src/schema.sql:163` is unconditional:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_chunks_embedding ON content_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
```

`src/core/postgres-engine.ts` does call `getPostgresSchema(dims, model)` with what should be the templated dim, but as @metaWuming hypothesized, either (a) `gw.getEmbeddingDimensions()` returns the default 1536 because the gateway hasn't read the runtime config yet, or (b) `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` runs before the policy can swap that line. The error throws before `sqlText` reaches the connection, matching (b).

Worth noting: `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts:84-87` and `embeddingMismatchMessage` already know to emit a skip-comment when dims > 2000 — same logic just needs to reach the bootstrap path.

Adding one concrete use case from Kimi / Moonshot AI.

Kimi is not Anthropic-compatible at the API-shape level; it is an OpenAI-compatible provider. But capability-wise, current Kimi models are clearly in the class of agent-capable frontier models: long-context reasoning, tool use, multi-step planning, and parallel agent workflows.

So I think the right abstraction here should be capability-based rather than provider-name-based.

Instead of:

```ts
isAnthropicProvider(model)
```

or a hard-coded allowlist of Anthropic-like provider prefixes, GBrain could route subagent eligibility through the provider recipe metadata, for example:

```ts
recipe.touchpoints.chat.supports_subagent_loop === true
```

That would let each provider recipe make an explicit claim about whether it supports the subagent loop contract, while still keeping the safety guard. Providers that are merely OpenAI-compatible for basic chat would remain excluded. Providers with validated agent/tool-loop behavior could opt in.

Related narrow provider request: #1219 adds Kimi / Moonshot as a chat + expansion provider first, with `supports_subagent_loop: false` initially. If this issue lands, Kimi could then be evaluated separately for subagent support without coupling the provider recipe work to the subagent abstraction work.

+1 on making dream synthesis and subagent LLM calls go through the provider/helper abstraction rather than being Anthropic-coupled.

A concrete downstream case: Hermes + GBrain deployments may want to use Kimi / Moonshot for most GBrain reasoning surfaces while keeping retrieval on ZeroEntropy. The desired routing looks like:

```bash
gbrain config set models.expansion kimi:kimi-k2.6
gbrain config set models.chat kimi:kimi-k2.6
gbrain config set facts.extraction_model kimi:kimi-k2.6
gbrain config set models.dream.synthesize kimi:kimi-k2.6
```

This works conceptually for the normal chat/expansion/synthesis surfaces, but dream/subagent internals are harder to reason about when any path bypasses the provider abstraction or assumes Anthropic-specific API behavior.

I think the clean split is:

1. Provider recipes declare capabilities: chat, expansion, tools, prompt cache, subagent loop compatibility, max context, etc.
2. Dream synthesis and subagent workers call through a provider-neutral helper/gateway.
3. Anthropic-specific optimizations such as prompt caching stay behind capability checks, not hard-coded call paths.

This would let deployments use OpenAI-compatible agent models where appropriate while preserving Anthropic-specific behavior when it is actually required.

Related narrow provider request: #1219 adds Kimi / Moonshot as a chat + expansion provider first. It intentionally does not claim subagent support until the provider/helper boundary is ready and the tool-loop behavior can be validated.

## Update — body placement isn't enough either

Followed my own workaround and added the phrase to the markdown body as `**Canonical GBrain search phrase:** \`<phrase>\``. Confirmed via grep that it's in the body. Re-synced. Still misses.

Digging deeper, the issue isn't just frontmatter scoping — it's that hyphen-concatenated identifier-style phrases like:

```
dr-payables-usd-2026-05-19-quechibot-canonical
caja-bento-scoped-keys-2026-05-20-quechibot-canonical
```

don't match as literal strings, even when present in the body. The same page is reachable by natural-language queries like `"scoped api keys replit"` or `"caja bento scoped keys 2026"`.

Looks like the tokenizer is splitting on hyphens (so each token becomes `dr`, `payables`, `usd`, `2026`, etc.) but then BM25/vector match against the concatenated identifier as a whole fails because no chunk surface preserves the full identifier as one token, AND the individual tokens are too common to rank the right page first.

## Refined ask

Two things would help:

1. **Index frontmatter scalar values** (original ask).
2. **Preserve identifier-style phrases as searchable tokens.** Either:
   - Add an alternate tokenization pass that keeps hyphenated identifiers intact (e.g. anything matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,}` as a literal token in addition to the split tokens), or
   - Index a normalized `phrase-id` form derived from anchors/code spans in the body (e.g. inline `\`code\`` spans become indexed literally).

The second approach (treating inline `\`code\`` spans as literal-search tokens) feels like the cleanest behavioral fix because it gives authors an explicit way to opt a phrase into literal search just by wrapping it in backticks.

## Workaround for now

Receipts ship two phrases:
- A literal identifier in backticks for structured cross-reference.
- A natural-language phrase ("Caja Bento finance agent access handoff 2026-05-20") that the existing chunker handles fine for human verification.
